subject: TenantLabs API decoupling: discovery recap & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Kim <alyssa@tenantlabs.io>, Evan Brooks <evan.brooks@tenantlabs.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: TenantLabs API decoupling: discovery recap & next steps

Hi Alyssa / Evan —

Thanks for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call so we can align on next steps. High level: TenantLabs wants to reduce dependency on hosted proprietary LLM APIs (OpenAI / Anthropic) while keeping current UX for chat and embeddings intact. Below are the notes I captured; please correct me where I’m off.

Top pain points you shared
- Token spend and unpredictable per-month costs driven by high-volume chat usage (search + summarization flows).
- Compliance: need for audit logs and option for VPC/on-prem for sensitive customer data.
- Behavioral drift: model output variability across vendors and occasional hallucinations impacting SLA for automated summaries.
- Latency spikes on long-context sessions (esp. >8k tokens) — impacts page load and interactive editors.

Current stack (as I heard it)
- Node.js backend (AWS ECS) calling OpenAI Chat completions + Anthropic for higher-safety prompts.
- Vector DB: managed (Pinecone) for retrieval-augmented generation.
- Fine-tuned prompts and a small set of lightweight post-processing heuristics in backend.

Success criteria for a migration/POC
- Functionality: parity on top-3 intents (search, summarize, follow-up extraction) within +/-3% of current precision/recall.
- Latency: p95 < 600ms at current per-instance traffic profile (we measured ~450ms baseline, spikes to 1.4s).
- Cost: target reduction of token-equivalent cost by at least 40% for steady-state traffic.
- Ops/Security: must support VPC-private deployment or dedicated tenancy, and provide access to request-level audit logs.

Initial model shortlist we discussed (for POC)
- Llama 2.1 chat (7B / 13B) — good instruction-following baseline.
- Mistral Instruct family — promising latency/quality tradeoff.
- MosaicML MPT-7B Instruct — compatible with current tokenizer and faster quantized runs.
- Note: you’ll still have Anthropic for high-safety flows during transition; goal is to reduce reliance, not immediate 1:1 replacement.

Technical blockers called out
- Tokenizer compatibility with your fine-tuned prompts and post-processing (you mentioned explicit token offsets).
- Embeddings parity for semantic search — need a drop-in or migration plan for vector space alignment.
- Streaming & function/tool-calling parity for in-editor features.

Next steps (proposed)
1) TenantLabs: share security questionnaire + a small sample of prompt/response pairs (sanitized) — we’ll use these for evaluation.
2) Redwood: provide a compatibility matrix + recommended model/config combos, and run a 2-week POC with two model variants (benchmarked for cost/latency/quality).
3) Schedule a technical kickoff with your engineering + security teams (30–45m) — propose week of Jun 14.
4) Procurement: Marissa will send a preliminary SOW and procurement checklist so we can map timelines.

Attachments: Tenant security questionnaire (you asked us to start), and a compatibility matrix stub for model/tokenizer notes.

If that all looks right I’ll queue the POC plan and Marissa will follow up with the SOW + calendar invite.

Thanks again — excited to help TenantLabs lower costs while keeping the product reliable.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0182

Subject: Re: TenantLabs API decoupling: discovery recap & next steps

Hi Ben —

Thanks for the tidy summary — this matches what we discussed. A couple of clarifications from our side:

Stack details
- Backend: Node (Express) microservice that calls OpenAI ChatCompletion (gpt-4o) for conversational flows and Anthropic Claude for safety-critical summarization.
- Embeddings: currently using OpenAI text-embedding-3-large; indexed in Pinecone with cosine similarity.
- We have a small fine-tune-ish layer: collection of prompt templates and a few calibrated system messages we pass server-side.

Evaluation priorities
- Embedding cosine preservation: we need minimal re-indexing pain — ideally a migration path where we can do rolling re-indexing without search downtime.
- Tokenization: we rely on exact token offsets for our highlight/highlight-to-source feature. If tokenizer changes, we need tooling to map offsets reliably.
- Safety: for now we want to continue Anthropic in a hybrid model until we validate the open models’ safety for sensitive summaries.

Procurement timeline
- Procurement kickoff: target end of Q3 (Sept) — procurement team will need the SOW and estimated TCO to start internal approvals.

We’ll share the sanitized examples this afternoon (redacted text + replaced PII) and our security questionnaire in a single package.

Two asks from you before we kickoff POC:
1) A short note on how Redwood handles tokenizer mismatches and mapping offsets (even at a high level).
2) A sample benchmarking plan (what metrics you’ll capture during the 2-week POC).

Appreciate it — looking forward to the POC.

—Alyssa
Alyssa Kim
Director, Product 
TenantLabs

Alyssa — great, thanks for the details and the asks. Quick replies inline: 

1) Tokenizer mismatches: we’ll provide a tokenizer-mapping utility as part of the POC. High level: for common model families we expose tokenization metadata and a mapping layer that can translate offsets between tokenizers (best-effort) and a small test harness you run against your sanitized prompt/response pairs. For hard cases we recommend using the token-index + character-offset alignment tool we include; Marissa will attach the doc.

2) Benchmark plan (summary):
- Quality: intent precision/recall on your sample set, BLEU-like fidelity checks for summary tasks, and manual review on a ~50-sample stratified set.
- Latency: per-request time (p50/p95) with same traffic profile as your service; measure cold vs warm KV cache.
- Cost: tokenized usage vs measured inference cost for each candidate model and quantization setting.
- Stability: run 24h continuous stress on typical retrieval lengths (2k/6k/10k tokens) to look for drift and spikes.

I’ll have Marissa drop the POC plan + SOW and propose Fri, Jun 18 for the technical kickoff (30m). If that works we’ll lock calendar times.

Thanks — Ben

Hi Alyssa — forwarding a short technical checklist for your engineers to review before the kickoff. If you prefer, we can include a short pre-kickoff spike (1 day) where our SEs run a tokenizer/embedding parity check on your sanitized data.

Technical checklist (short)
- Provide 200 sanitized prompt/response pairs + 200 embedding vectors (or the raw text to re-embed)
- Confirm vector DB snapshot window and whether we can run a rolling reindex during off-peak hours
- Confirm whether your current system relies on OpenAI-specific metadata (e.g., response.usage.token_counts) — we can adapt to a normalized usage shim but want to know upfront
- If you use tool-calling / structured JSON outputs, share one example schema and any validation rules

SE notes (for POC)
- We’ll run two canonical configs: 1) Llama2-13B quantized + prefix KV cache; 2) Mistral-Instruct tuned 7B with aggressive batching.
- For embeddings: trial re-embedding of a 10k doc subset and compute cosine preservation against your current index.
- Streaming: we’ll validate chunked output and tool-call emulation for the editor flow.

I’ll attach the compatibility matrix and a short guide for the tokenizer mapping utility. Ben / Grace will follow up with calendar invites and the SOW.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
